_meta.purpose: Recurring mistranslation traps for the Poweradmin gettext catalogues, mined from the machine-translation repair sweep.
_meta.scope: Wrong-meaning classes. Literals that must never be translated live in scripts/dnt_glossary.json and are not repeated here.

mined_from.repair_commits: every commit touching locale/*/LC_MESSAGES/messages.po since 2026-07-15, parsed with scripts/poutil.py
mined_from.pending_review: the OUT_<locale>_NN.json corrections from the per-entry review queue

_meta.universal: English source words whose wrong sense was picked in several unrelated languages, plus the structural failure classes. locale_count is what to sort by: it says which trap to check first.
_meta.per_locale: Confirmed bad renderings for one language. Each rule is the (guard, pattern, replacement) shape that scripts/apply_locale_corrections.py applies: guard.include and guard.exclude are matched case-insensitively against the English msgid, pattern and replace against the msgstr. A rule is only listed where the same wrong rendering occurred more than once.
_meta.review_only: Substitutions that cannot be made safe. Report these to a human; never apply them.
_meta.path_safety: ASCII patterns are wrapped in (?<![/\\\w-]) ... (?![/\\\w-]) rather than \b, because \b treats '/' as a boundary and a \b-anchored rule once rewrote the literal path templates/emails/custom/. Acronym rules use (?<![A-Za-z0-9]) ... (?![A-Za-z0-9]) instead, so a trailing hyphen in DNSEC-signeret still matches while AAA stays out of AAAA.

structural.what: A negation is lost, added, or the message is replaced by its opposite. The result reads perfectly naturally, which is why it survives review.
structural.detect: Compare the polarity of the msgstr with the msgid. Check antonym msgid pairs (Set as default / Unset as default, Server Running / Server Not Running, Sign Zone / Unsign Zone, Enabled / Disabled) - if two opposite msgids share one msgstr, one of them is wrong.

structural.what: An uppercase NO or NOT in the source is copied through untranslated while the surrounding verb is left affirmative, so the sentence asserts the opposite and ends in a stray English word.
A msgid that ends in ': ' has its trailing space trimmed. The caller appends a detail string at runtime, so the detail runs into the colon.
structural.detect: msgid endswith whitespace and msgstr does not end with the same run. 32 msgids in the template end in a trailing space.
structural.fix: apply_locale_corrections.py --trailing (restore_trailing_whitespace) is safe to run unattended; the source's own trailing run is authoritative.

structural.what: A deliberately unfinished fragment gains terminal punctuation. '(ID' becomes '(ID)' and 'Are you sure you want to delete' gains a question mark, so the value appended at runtime lands after the closing paren or the '?'.
structural.detect: msgid has unbalanced brackets or no terminal punctuation while the msgstr closes or terminates it.

structural.what: RFC keywords lose their force. MUST / MUST NOT / SHOULD NOT / REQUIRED / NOT RECOMMENDED become plain statements, and the uppercase CRITICAL: / IMPORTANT: / WARNING: / NOTE: prefix is dropped or downgraded.
structural.detect: msgid contains an all-caps keyword; check the msgstr carries an equivalent emphasis, and that a leading 'CRITICAL:'-style prefix survives.

structural.what: A message collapses to a fragment. 'Issue Wildcard' became just 'Card'; 'Forward Zones' became 'Vazhdo' (Continue); multi-sentence warnings lose every clause but one.
structural.detect: msgstr is drastically shorter than the msgid, or a multi-sentence msgid maps to a single short noun phrase.

structural.what: The engine repeats a word or the whole translation. 'Type' became 'Cineal Cineal Cineal Cineal' in ga_IE; ms_MY repeated words mid-sentence throughout.
structural.fix: apply_locale_corrections.py already carries collapse rules for ga_IE and ms_MY.

structural.what: A protocol name is corrupted by one or two characters, so it still looks like an acronym but names nothing.
structural.detect: Every literal in scripts/dnt_glossary.json must survive byte-identical. A near-miss is the case where the literal is absent but a string within edit distance 1-2 of it is present.

structural.what: A protocol name is rewritten in the target script, which no longer names the protocol and no longer matches anything the user can search for.
observed: hi_IN: SRV -> एसआरवी, NSEC -> एनईसी, DMARC -> डीएमएआरसी, TSIG -> टीएसआईजी
structural.fix: scripts/dnt_glossary.json 'literal' list is the enforceable set.

structural.what: Config keys, table names, file paths and format examples are translated or have their separators spaced out, sending users to something that does not exist. Example addresses and xx-xx-xx-xx-xx-xx templates get extra groups.

The msgstr is fluent text that belongs to a different message, or to no part of this application at all. 'Native' was rendered as 'Backup frequency' in sv_SE, 'Invalid CNAME configuration.' in id_ID and 'Record appears to be using saliency maps.' in uk_UA.
structural.detect: No mechanical rule catches this. It needs a per-entry read against the English source.

structural.what: Placeholders and markup are altered: a stray capital Z welded onto %s / %d, %1$s reordered away, <code> tags dropped, [BRACKET_TOKENS] translated.
structural.fix: apply_locale_corrections.py --placeholders strips the Z leak; composer locale:check fails on real format-spec breakage.

structural.what: The engine emitted a related language or the wrong national standard: Indonesian vocabulary throughout ms_MY, Croatian forms in bs_BA, Mainland Chinese words in zh_TW, European Portuguese phrasing in pt_BR.
structural.fix: apply_locale_corrections.py already carries the vocabulary tables.

structural.what: The same English term is rendered two or three different ways across the catalogue. Not wrong, but it makes the UI read as if written by three people.
structural.detect: Count the renderings of 'record', 'zone', 'key' and 'template' per locale and pick the dominant one.
